title: shutdown
summary: Ask running engines (lsp, cycles --fix, index, lint-all) to stand down cleanly, so an index can be rebuilt or an engine replaced
intro: Read this when you need to rebuild an index that running engines hold open, or replace a running engine: shutdown asks the running engines (lsp, cycles --fix, and the long index and lint-all runs) to close their stores and stand down, without killing them (only --force terminates an engine that does not answer). An index run stops between files with its database consistent and the same command resumes; the installer and build\stage-engine.ps1 use this channel first.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint shutdown [--db <file.sqlite>]... [--wait <sec>] [--dry-run] [--all] [--force] (ask running engines to stand down: close every store, exit 0; `index` and `lint-all` runs exit 4)
help: drag-lint shutdown [--db <file.sqlite>]... [--wait <sec>] [--dry-run] [--all] [--force]   (ask running engines to stand down: close every store, exit 0; `index` and `lint-all` runs exit 4)
transport: a Windows NAMED PIPE, never a TCP port -- \\.\pipe\drag-lint-ctl-<sid>-s<session>-p<pid>, created with an
explicit DACL for the creating user only, so another user or session cannot signal your engines. Engines in

`lsp`, `cycles --fix`, `index` (incl. --all) and `lint-all` mode listen (`serve` and other one-shot verbs do not): an index run stops between files, database consistent, same command resumes; lint-all prints PARTIAL findings. --all (the default) asks every
reachable engine; --db keeps only engines holding that index; --dry-run lists them and changes nothing.
--wait (default 5 s) bounds the graceful wait per engine: one inside a request answers BUSY and keeps
running (exit 1). --force TerminateProcess'es ONLY an engine that refused or did not answer, and says
ESCALATING when it does. Every honoured or refused request is audited on the engine's stderr and in
